briefing.title: Briefing after cycle 011 — what the world is pressing on

lines.text: UCDP counted about 244,600 people killed in organised violence in 2025, up from about 187,000 in 2024, and a record 65 state-based conflicts.
lines.say: The Uppsala Conflict Data Program counted about two hundred and forty-four thousand six hundred people killed in organised violence in twenty twenty-five, up from about one hundred and eighty-seven thousand in twenty twenty-four, and a record sixty-five state-based conflicts.

lines.text: SIPRI put world military spending at $2,887 billion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms.
lines.say: SIPRI put world military spending at two thousand eight hundred and eighty-seven billion dollars in twenty twenty-five, up two point nine percent in real terms.

lines.text: UNODC puts the world's homicide rate at 5.1 per 100,000 people in 2024, down from 5.9 in 2015.
lines.say: The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime puts the world's homicide rate at five point one per hundred thousand people in twenty twenty-four, down from five point nine in twenty fifteen.

lines.text: Iran announced a prohibited zone around the Strait of Hormuz on 5 September.
lines.say: Iran announced a prohibited zone around the Strait of Hormuz on the fifth of September.

lines.text: In mid-October, ship traffic through the strait stood about 70 percent below its pre-war level.
lines.say: In the middle of October, ship traffic through the strait stood about seventy percent below its pre-war level.

lines.text: Preliminary estimates put oil flows, with transfers at sea, at about 82 percent of pre-war levels.
lines.say: Preliminary estimates put oil flows, with transfers at sea, at about eighty-two percent of pre-war levels.

lines.text: The IMF sees 4.7 percent inflation in 2026, hardest for energy importers outside the technology chain.
lines.say: The International Monetary Fund sees four point seven percent inflation in twenty twenty-six, hardest for energy importers outside the technology chain.

lines.text: In the Philippines, which imports about 98 percent of its oil from the Middle East, a state think tank estimated in April that 1.3 to 3.1 million people could be pushed into poverty.
lines.say: In the Philippines, which imports about ninety-eight percent of its oil from the Middle East, a state think tank estimated in April that one point three to three point one million people could be pushed into poverty.

lines.text: SOFI 2026 nowcasts 645 million people undernourished in 2025 (7.8%, range 608–696 million), about 14 million fewer than in 2024.
lines.say: The State of Food Security report nowcasts six hundred and forty-five million people undernourished in twenty twenty-five, seven point eight percent, in a range of six hundred and eight to six hundred and ninety-six million, about fourteen million fewer than in twenty twenty-four.

lines.text: Separately, 266 million people in 47 food-crisis countries and territories faced high acute food insecurity in 2025, 22.9% of those analysed.
lines.say: Separately, two hundred and sixty-six million people in forty-seven food-crisis countries and territories faced high acute food insecurity in twenty twenty-five, twenty-two point nine percent of those analysed.

lines.text: The World Bank nowcasts about 811 million people, 1 in 10, below $3.00 a day (2021 PPP) in 2026; 2024, the latest year with sufficient data, stands at 824 million.
lines.say: The World Bank's now cast is about eight hundred and eleven million people, one in ten, below three dollars a day in twenty twenty-six; twenty twenty-four, the latest year with sufficient data, stands at eight hundred and twenty-four million.

lines.text: UNDP and OPHI count 1.2 billion (18.9%) in acute multidimensional poverty in 108 countries, surveys of 2014–2025.
lines.say: The United Nations Development Programme and Oxford's poverty initiative count one point two billion people, eighteen point nine percent, in acute multidimensional poverty in one hundred and eight countries, in surveys from twenty fourteen to twenty twenty-five.

channels.title: Debt, work and cost of living

lines.text: UN Trade and Development counts 3.7 billion people in 51 developing countries that spend more on interest than on either health or education.
lines.say: UN Trade and Development counts three point seven billion people, in fifty-one developing countries, that spend more on interest than on either health or education.

lines.text: Developing countries paid $995 billion in net interest on public debt in 2025.
lines.say: Developing countries paid nine hundred and ninety-five billion dollars in net interest on public debt in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: The ILO counts nearly 300 million workers in extreme working poverty and 2.1 billion in informal work.
lines.say: The International Labour Organization counts nearly three hundred million workers in extreme working poverty, and two point one billion in informal work.

sources.label: UN Trade and Development, A World of Debt, 2026 edition

lines.text: World Inequality Lab estimates, 2025: the global top 10% took 53% of income and held 75% of wealth, the bottom half 8% and 2%.
lines.say: World Inequality Lab estimates for twenty twenty-five: the global top ten percent took fifty-three percent of income and held seventy-five percent of wealth, the bottom half eight percent and two percent.

lines.text: The top 0.001% held nearly 6.1% of wealth, up from around 3.8% in 1995.
lines.say: The top zero point zero zero one percent held nearly six point one percent of wealth, up from around three point eight percent in nineteen ninety-five.

lines.text: Average income in North America & Oceania is about 13 times Sub-Saharan Africa's.
lines.say: Average income in North America and Oceania is about thirteen times Sub-Saharan Africa's.

lines.text: About 50,000 women and girls were killed by partners or family members in 2024, UN Women and UNODC estimate.
lines.say: About fifty thousand women and girls were killed by partners or family members in twenty twenty-four, UN Women and UNODC estimate.

lines.text: Forbes counted a record 3,428 billionaires worth an estimated $20.1 trillion at 1 March 2026 prices, 400 more people and up from $16.1 trillion in its 2025 list.
lines.say: Forbes counted a record three thousand four hundred and twenty-eight billionaires worth an estimated twenty point one trillion dollars at prices of the first of March twenty twenty-six, four hundred more people, and up from sixteen point one trillion dollars in its twenty twenty-five list.

lines.text: Epoch AI estimates five hyperscalers held 71% of the world's cumulative AI compute in Q4 2025, up from 63% in Q1 2024.
lines.say: Epoch AI estimates that five hyperscalers held seventy-one percent of the world's cumulative AI compute in the last quarter of twenty twenty-five, up from sixty-three percent in the first quarter of twenty twenty-four.

lines.text: September 2026 was 1.63°C above pre-industrial and the 12 months to it 1.50°C; the month was the second-warmest September in Copernicus's ERA5 record.
lines.say: September twenty twenty-six was one point six three degrees Celsius above pre-industrial, and the twelve months to it one point five zero degrees; the month was the second-warmest September in the Copernicus record.

lines.text: EM-DAT recorded 358 natural-hazard disasters, 16,607 deaths and 110.2 million people affected in 2025, figures still evolving.
lines.say: The EM-DAT disaster database recorded three hundred and fifty-eight natural-hazard disasters, sixteen thousand six hundred and seven deaths and one hundred and ten point two million people affected in twenty twenty-five, figures still evolving.

lines.text: NOAA puts the central Pacific at 2.1 degrees above normal.
lines.say: NOAA puts the central Pacific at two point one degrees above normal.

lines.text: A strong to very strong El Niño is likely into early 2027.
lines.say: A strong to very strong El Niño is likely into early twenty twenty-seven.

lines.text: NOAA puts the odds of a historic peak of 2.5 degrees at 83 percent for October to December, and 70 for November to January.
lines.say: NOAA puts the odds of a historic peak of two and a half degrees at eighty-three percent for October to December, and seventy for November to January.

lines.text: It lands on oceans that set a September record, in a month 1.63 degrees above pre-industrial.
lines.say: It lands on oceans that set a September record, in a month one point six three degrees above pre-industrial.

lines.text: COP31 meets in Antalya from 9 to 20 November.
lines.say: Cop thirty-one meets in Antalya, from the ninth to the twentieth of November.

lines.text: Current policies lead to about 2.8 degrees this century, full national pledges to about 2.6.
lines.say: Current policies lead to about two point eight degrees this century. Full national pledges, to about two point six.

lines.text: The lowest path that overshoots 1.5 degrees needs cuts of 18 percent by 2030.
lines.say: The lowest path that overshoots one and a half degrees needs cuts of eighteen percent by twenty thirty.

lines.text: The pledges deliver 5 to 8.
lines.say: The pledges deliver five to eight.

lines.text: As of July, finance and adaptation remained stalled.

lines.text: Air pollution contributed to about 7.9 million deaths in 2023, the State of Global Air estimates.
lines.say: Air pollution contributed to about seven point nine million deaths in twenty twenty-three, the State of Global Air estimates.

lines.text: In 2024, 2.1 billion people lacked safely managed drinking water and 3.4 billion safely managed sanitation.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-four, two point one billion people lacked safely managed drinking water, and three point four billion, safely managed sanitation.

lines.text: The Living Planet Index records an average decline of 73 percent since 1970.
lines.say: The Living Planet Index records an average decline of seventy-three percent since nineteen seventy.

lines.text: It rests on 35,803 population trends of 5,790 vertebrate species.
lines.say: It rests on thirty-five thousand, eight hundred and three population trends, of five thousand, seven hundred and ninety vertebrate species.

lines.text: 95 percent in Latin America and the Caribbean.
lines.say: Ninety-five percent in Latin America and the Caribbean.

lines.text: 85 percent in fresh water.
lines.say: Eighty-five percent in fresh water.

lines.text: UN IGME estimates 4.9 million children died before age five in 2024, down from 6.1 million in 2015, and the pace of decline has slowed by 61%.
lines.say: The United Nations child mortality group estimates four point nine million children died before age five in twenty twenty-four, down from six point one million in twenty fifteen, and the pace of decline has slowed by sixty-one percent.

lines.text: DR Congo's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak reached 10,414 confirmed cases, including 5,372 deaths, by 30 October 2026 (INSP).
lines.say: Congo's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak reached ten thousand four hundred and fourteen confirmed cases, including five thousand three hundred and seventy-two deaths, by the thirtieth of October twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: The Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in Congo: 10,274 confirmed cases and 4,992 deaths by 29 October.
lines.say: The Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, in Congo. Ten thousand, two hundred and seventy-four confirmed cases, and four thousand, nine hundred and ninety-two deaths, by the twenty-ninth of October.

lines.text: That is more than twice the cases of early August.
Kenya has nine confirmed cases, and Nigeria reported one in October.
lines.say: Kenya has nine confirmed cases, and Nigeria reported one in October.

lines.text: No licensed vaccine exists for this strain.
In Kenya, contact tracing is partly on paper.
The EU and EEA recorded 1,715 West Nile infections by 7 October, the most ever reported there, and 130 deaths.
lines.say: The European Union and the European Economic Area recorded one thousand, seven hundred and fifteen West Nile infections by the seventh of October, the most ever reported there, and one hundred and thirty deaths.

lines.text: Nigeria counted 18,334 suspected cases of diphtheria and 731 deaths by week 34.
lines.say: Nigeria counted eighteen thousand, three hundred and thirty-four suspected cases of diphtheria, and seven hundred and thirty-one deaths, by week thirty-four.

lines.text: How much of this is climate, and how much is lost surveillance and vaccination, is still open.

lines.say: The V-Dem Institute's best estimate is ninety-two autocracies and eighty-seven democracies at the end of twenty twenty-five, with seventy-four percent of people, six billion, living in autocracies, up from fifty percent in two thousand and five.

lines.text: Freedom House recorded a 20th consecutive year of decline in global freedom in 2025: 54 countries down, 35 up.
lines.say: Freedom House recorded a twentieth consecutive year of decline in global freedom in twenty twenty-five: fifty-four countries down, thirty-five up.

lines.say: The twenty twenty-six index of Reporters Without Borders, covering twenty twenty-five, rates press freedom difficult or very serious in fifty-two point two percent of one hundred and eighty countries and territories, against thirteen point seven percent in two thousand and two.

lines.text: In the 2026 Digital News Report survey, trust in news averaged 37% across 48 markets, the lowest since measuring began in 2015.
lines.say: In the twenty twenty-six Digital News Report survey, trust in news averaged thirty-seven percent across forty-eight markets, the lowest since measuring began in twenty fifteen.

lines.text: US payroll data show no widespread displacement, but employment at ages 22–25 in highly AI-exposed occupations was about 19% below the pace of less-exposed peers by June 2026; descriptive, not causal.

lines.say: In American payroll data, employment of workers aged twenty-two to twenty-five, in the jobs most exposed to AI, stands about nineteen percent behind less exposed peers.
